analysis:
Both changed files are documentation only (docs/architecture/hardware-support.md and docs/architecture/inference.md), so no code, authorization, attestation, encryption or protocol behavior changes in this PR. I found no concrete security regression.

Checked against the threat model:
- hardware-support.md lines 35-41 say Local HTTP Responses keeps host-side JSON. The continuation-history LRU is bounded, but the SDK response-object store has no matching eviction. This is a plaintext-retention and memory-growth note for A-001 and for availability. It documents existing behavior and is not shown to be new. The owning doc, provider/direct-mode.md, was not supplied, so the stated limits were not verified. Later passes may want to check whether this is a gap in the T-014/T-028 text.
- hardware-support.md lines 109-148 and inference.md lines 71-310 describe GLM5Next admission, memory pricing, fail-closed retention after an unproven retirement, template pinning and identity-chain checks. These are consistent with fail-closed memory and ownership posture (T-027 on weight identity, T-010 on in-flight work). They are claims about code that was not supplied, so none could be verified. They state that synthetic tests do not establish output parity or qualification, and that local qualification cannot bypass managed load.
- inference.md changes to the SlotFactory row say a refused SSD store's typed reason reaches the bridge for local /metrics only. This is consistent with T-041, since nothing is sent to the coordinator and no new at-rest artifact is introduced. The text does not change SSD TTL, HMAC naming or the scope gate.
- inference.md also documents MiMo original-tool-schema restoration, rejection of client-supplied reserved schema metadata, GLM tool-suffix validation at end of stream, and a fixed shutdown log with no error payload. All are defensive or neutral.

Coverage limits: the inference.md patch excerpt is bounded, the referenced Swift sources were not supplied, and the TB-011 / TB-002 / TB-007 text was only indexed. No claim here has been checked against code.
